const US_INFO_HTML="

Scientific scope and review status

AGHIP — Analysis of Geospace and High-frequency Ionospheric Propagation
An integrated computational framework for HF/VHF/EME radio propagation and space-weather analysis.

Candidate for independent evaluation — not certified. Passing automated tests does not establish predictive accuracy, full ITU-R conformity or absence of defects.

How to interpret the panels

  • HF / Radio listening: monthly-median model under declared station assumptions. Path formulas cover short, interpolated and long-distance regimes; the implementation retains documented text/reference-code differences. P.1240 operational MUF, circuit reliability and a full ITURHFProp golden-master comparison are not claimed.
  • Antennas and noise: ideal elevation patterns with the same peak reference are an illustrative pattern comparison, not realized gain or directional noise rejection. NEC decks, losses, ground and orientation are still needed for actual installations. P.372 describes climatology; S/N sensitivity is assumption-based, not a statistical confidence interval.
  • VHF / LF / MF / 160 m: VHF indices are uncalibrated screening. LF/MF use an experimental P.1147 annual-median profile between 150 and 1,700 kHz; the Figure 4 comparison remains open and ground wave is not calculated. On 160 m, WSPR evidence and geometry are separate from the conditional measured-reception experiment. P.1147 is not extended to 160 m.
  • EME: geometric Moon visibility and polarization context use approximate ephemerides. Faraday severity is contextual, not measured path TEC. Global lunar phase and eclipse dates are distinct from local visibility.
  • Weather: INMET for BR, NWS for US, ECCC for CA, within the selected operational layer. Unavailable or incomplete feeds do not mean no alerts. Radar shows precipitation; GLM shows satellite total-lightning flashes, not verified ground strikes. P.453 uses a local forecast column, not the entire radio path.
  • Observations: GIRO assimilation remains experimental. WSPR is an opportunistic received-spot sample; missing spots cannot establish non-reception. Global solar/geomagnetic indices are not measurements made at the grid.

P.533 profile and documented choices

Table 1a MUF points are separate from Table 1b screening points. Screening is limited to 4,000 km following §4 and the inspected official routine; the broader range printed in Table 1b is retained as an unresolved text discrepancy. All required control points must be available. Screening geometry follows §5.1, while discrete field-mode height follows §5.2.1. Polynomial G includes the published +90.47xr term. fL in the long-path expression is a model parameter, not an invented hard cutoff. Lm/Lz and absorption averaging retain the declared reference-code profile.

ITU-R P.533-14 · P.1239 · P.372 · P.453 · ITU-R reference source · WMM

Reproducible checks

The release report states exactly which tests ran. Embedded WMM and noise checks cover their supplied reference cases only. No external specialist approval is implied.

validarP533Blindagem() · validarWMM() · validarP372()

WSPR observational campaign

Records are grouped by the application-script hash. These opportunistic residuals are not an unbiased test of detection probability.

Single-file operation

Core libraries, equations, coefficients and the overview world outline are embedded. Internet is still required for current API data, street tiles, radar and the GLM HDF5 decoder. Offline operation is not a source of live weather warnings. CORS restrictions belong to each provider and cannot be overridden by this HTML.
